primary_diagnosis_treated: Uncontrolled Essential Hypertension with Stage 5 CKD and Atherogenic Dyslipidaemia

medications.dose: 1.25 mg once daily (½ tablet) – titrate by 1.25‑2.5 mg every 2‑4 weeks to target 5 mg daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Lower blood pressure; provide renal protection in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line therapy for hypertension in CKD (step 1) and advises careful titration with renal monitoring

medications.duration: Lifelong — add if BP >140/90 mmHg after 4‑6 weeks on maximally tolerated ramipril
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive to achieve target BP in CKD patients ≥55 y
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends CCB as preferred add‑on for patients ≥55 y or with CKD (step 2)

medications.dose: 80 mg once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C and cardiovascular risk in CKD/atherogenic dyslipidaemia
medications.nice_justification: CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin for all adults with IHD or CKD not on dialysis

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily, titrate up to 80 mg daily (or divided BID) based on congestion
medications.duration: Lifelong while fluid overload persists — review electrolytes and renal function after each titration
medications.purpose: Manage volume overload in stage 5 CKD (thiazides ineffective when eGFR < 30)
medications.nice_justification: NG136 advises loop diuretic for symptomatic fluid overload in CKD

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing atorvastatin exposure ~2‑fold, raising risk of myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Consider using rosuvastatin 20 mg daily instead of atorvastatin, or start atorvastatin at 40 mg and monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium not provided – NICE NG136 requires K⁺ ≤5.0 mmol/L before starting ACE‑I and regular monitoring
Liver function tests not available – required before initiating high‑intensity statin per CG126
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio not recorded – ACE‑I benefit is greater with proteinuria, but still appropriate for BP control
QRISK 10‑year ASCVD risk not calculated – CKD with LDL‑C >160 mg/dL meets statin indication regardless of QRISK
No documented heart failure – ACE‑I and CCB are safe; if HF later diagnosed, avoid verapamil/diltiazem
No allergy history – must confirm no ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily with careful renal and potassium monitoring, titrating to 5 mg as tolerated. Add amlodipine 5 mg daily if BP remains above target after 4‑6 weeks. Initiate high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg nightly to address LDL‑C 161 mg/dL, with liver function monitoring. Consider furosemide 20 mg daily only if the patient shows signs of fluid overload. All choices follow NICE NG136 for hypertension in CKD and CG126 for lipid management, with attention to drug interactions, renal function, and the patient’s complex social situation.
